thread:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — KV cache memory is creeping steadily on long contexts (32k). Observed about +120MB over 6h on a single worker, not reclaimed between large sessions.
perf-bot: nightly-perf-regression: p95 gen +3.8% | kv_mem +120MB (32k) | job=kv-heap-watchdog
Alex Kim: Can you paste the allocator histogram and current runtime config? My hunch is bucket skew + lots of small leftover holes from variable-sized KV writes.
Maya Patel: Here's the trimmed jemalloc-like histogram from the snapshot:
  size    count
  64      4821
  128     1732
  176     918  <-- unexpected mode
  256     412
  512     39
Also runtime conf snippet we use on Canary:
```
kv_cache_enabled: true
block_size: 256
evict_threshold: 0.75
compaction: {enabled: false}
```
Alex Kim: That 176 mode is suspicious — looks like our encoder pairs produce 176-192 byte entries for a lot of tokens in long contexts (KV headers + small payload). With block_size=256 we get a lot of partial fill and freelist fragmentation.
TJ: FWIW I ran a micro-sim last week with the same distribution. Changing block_size=128 dropped resident by ~40MB but increased CPU for allocator churn ~+2.1%. Tradeoff is CPU vs memory.
Sanjay Rao: Another lever: incremental compaction during low QPS windows. Rather than a full stop-the-world compact, we can drain freelist buckets incrementally and move live entries when eviction ratio < X. Sketch of compaction policy:
```
compaction: {
  enabled: true
  window_seconds: 30
  move_budget_per_window: 1000
  trigger_eviction_backlog_ratio: 0.2
}
```
Maya Patel: Nice. Could also try a hybrid bucket allocator: small buckets (64/128) for short entries, large buckets (256/512) for tail blobs. Means more complex free lists but lower internal waste.
Alex Kim: Agree. Two experiments to run: (A) block_size=128 baseline across 3 canaries, capture pprof/heap snapshots; (B) hybrid allocator prototype on a single canary with incremental compaction enabled. We should measure: resident, GC/compaction CPU, p95 latency, and eviction churn rate.
Maya Patel: I'll kick off (A) now on staging-3. Command I use to collect heap + allocator stats:
```
ssh staging-3
sudo pkill -USR1 runtime || true  # dumps heap profile to /tmp/heap-*.pprof
curl -s http://localhost:9100/debug/allocstats > /tmp/allocstats.txt
```
TJ: When you run (B) let's add a sampling flamegraph around the compaction worker to check impact on p99 latency. I can add the perf-record wrapper.
Sanjay Rao: One more thought: tune eviction policy to prioritize coalescing adjacent holes. If we bias eviction to choose keys that free adjacent slots, we can create longer contiguous free ranges for large entries. Cheap heuristic: prefer eviction candidates with adjacent_free_score > threshold.
Maya Patel: Good idea. Putting that in the experiment backlog. Running (A) now — will post results in ~2 hours. Anyone wants to jump on (B) prototype with me tomorrow?
Alex Kim: I'll pair for (B) tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
TJ: I'll prepare perf wrappers and the flamegraph job.
Maya Patel: Thanks — will update thread with raw snapshots and a short table of numbers (resident, eviction_rate, CPU) when done. :coffee:
